hook: SCP-5056 sets up a ghost story and then plays it as a workplace portrait: a Site-43 janitor and the scarred grey apparition that has trailed him through every mirror and lens for years. Much of the best material sits in the margins, in standing orders, signed staff notes and site bulletins, so give those as much attention as the main text. The experiment and incident reports are on a separate linked page that isn't part of this file.
whyItMatters:
The article flips the usual dynamic between the Foundation and its subject. The entity is grotesque and never lets up, yet the man it hounds has more or less made his peace with it, and the Site treats it like part of the building. It shows how a file can draw its weight from routine and tone rather than from danger.

The framing as a feed from the Site's internal network, with orders, bulletins and annotations from named doctors, makes the page feel like a workplace with its own history.
thingsToNotice: SCP-5056-A behaves as the exact opposite of whatever Deering needs: it gapes and shrieks when he tries to rest, and when he is low it lectures him about his blunders, his absent family, his hygiene and the pointlessness of people. Deering, for his part, has stopped flinching, praises its more inventive attacks with constructive notes, calls it Doug and refers to it as his Employee of the Month Award, a prize he has never won. That joke pays off in the bulletins, where the award is scrapped and its final recipient is a coworker honoured for reacting quickly during his cardiac episode, while the deterioration his early reviews predicted is noted as never having happened. The margin notes hint at friction among the researchers, with one doctor bristling at the idea that Deering might be causing the phenomenon and another questioning the ban on glasses after an unexplained incident involving the first. The SARGENT bulletin then spells out the stakes of his death, since a separated entity screams at 119 decibels across the Site, and the project wipes its members' memories every time they leave.
